title: Faking feature importance: A cautionary tale on the use of differentially-private synthetic data
summary: This paper empirically studies whether feature importance rankings derived from differentially-private synthetic data agree with those from the original data, using PrivBayes and PATE-CTGAN across artificial and real-world datasets. It finds that agreement is inconsistent and degrades under stronger privacy guarantees, cautioning against using DP synthetic data for exploratory feature engineering in sensitive domains like finance and healthcare. title: Fast, Accurate, and Simple Models for Tabular Data via Augmented Distillation
summary: The paper proposes FAST-DAD, a knowledge-distillation method that compresses complex AutoML ensemble predictors into single fast models by augmenting the training data via Gibbs sampling from a self-attention pseudolikelihood estimator. Across 30 tabular regression/classification datasets, this augmentation is compared against several alternative data-generation baselines for improving distilled student models. CTGAN, run using the original sdv-dev implementation, is one of the baseline data-augmentation methods evaluated against the authors' Gibbs-sampling approach.

title: Invertible Tabular GANs: Killing Two Birds with One Stone for Tabular Data Synthesis

To address rare/imbalanced binary features in their dataset, the authors trialed several synthetic data generation techniques and settled on CopulaGAN as the best trade-off between data coherence and computation time. title: Joint Distributional Learning via Cramer-Wold Distance
summary: This paper proposes a VAE-based generative model that uses a closed-form Cramer-Wold distance regularization and a two-step learning method to better align the aggregated posterior with the prior, aiming to improve joint distributional learning for high-dimensional tabular datasets with many categorical variables. The authors evaluate their approach's synthetic data generation performance against prior tabular synthesis methods discussed in related work. CTGAN is cited only in the related-work discussion, described as assuming continuous columns can be approximated via Gaussian mixture distributions to model the decoder, without being run in the experiments.

title: A Joint Synthetic Housing-Household Inventory
summary: This paper presents a framework for constructing a joint housing-household inventory that links synthetic individuals and households to compatible housing units from the National Structure Inventory, combining synthetic population generation, a deep contrastive learning compatibility model, and hierarchical optimization-based allocation, evaluated on coastal North Carolina. The authors adopt TabDiff, a diffusion-based tabular generator, as their synthesis engine, and benchmark it against TVAE and CTGAN implemented via the SDV library, which perform markedly worse on fidelity, correlation, and mode-collapse metrics. SDV's TVAE and CTGAN are run as rejected comparison baselines against the paper's chosen generative model.

title: KAXAI: An Integrated Environment for Knowledge Analysis and Explainable AI
summary: This paper presents KAXAI, an integrated software system combining AutoML, explainable-AI interpretation (via a proposed local interpreter called MEDLEY), and synthetic data generation into a single user-facing tool. For synthetic data generation the authors compare LLM-based generation, GAN-based dataset enhancement, and several Python synthetic-data libraries, finding GAN augmentation most reliable. The authors adopt CTGAN's mode-specific normalization scheme in their own model's representation of continuous attributes, and separately run TVAE as one of several state-of-the-art baseline generators (alongside DPCTGAN, DPWGAN, PATEGAN) reporting its statistical-utility and privacy-attack results in comparison tables. title: Knowledge-Guided Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Zero-Shot Psychiatric Data: Privacy Preserving Synthetic Data Generation
summary: This preprint proposes a zero-shot, knowledge-guided framework in which large language models, steered by Retrieval-Augmented Generation over DSM-5 and ICD-10 clinical criteria, generate synthetic psychiatric tabular data without training on real patient records. The method is evaluated on six anxiety-related disorders and compared for fidelity and privacy against real-data-trained deep generative baselines. title: LAB-Tab: LLM-Augmented Bayesian Network Adaptation for Few-Shot Tabular Generation
summary: This paper proposes LAB-Tab, a few-shot tabular data generation framework that fits a Bayesian network to a richer source-domain table, uses an LLM to propose plausible target-domain edges absent from the source graph, and calibrates these edges with a PPO policy before sampling target-domain tables. It is evaluated across six source-target distribution-shift scenarios built from US Census (ACS) tasks, where LAB-Tab is shown to outperform several baseline generators on distributional, utility, and dependency-preservation metrics. SDV's GaussianCopula and CopulaGAN synthesizers, along with CTGAN and TVAE, are run unmodified as baseline generators against which LAB-Tab's few-shot performance is benchmarked, with CTGAN singled out as the strongest baseline.

title: LAKEGEN: A LLM-based Tabular Corpus Generator for Evaluating Dataset Discovery in Data Lakes

The authors' prototype uses a general LLM to populate table values rather than a tabular GAN, but they note CTGAN as prior art and a possible future data-generation component. CTGAN is cited descriptively as the state-of-the-art conditional GAN approach for tabular data but is not run in the reported experiments.

title: Language Models are Realistic Tabular Data Generators
summary: This paper proposes GReaT, an auto-regressive large-language-model-based method that generates realistic synthetic tabular data by learning textual encodings of table rows and supports conditioning on arbitrary feature subsets. It benchmarks GReaT against CTGAN, TVAE, and CopulaGAN across multiple real-world tabular datasets using measures of data quality, discriminative similarity, and machine-learning efficacy. SDV's CopulaGAN, CTGAN, and TVAE are run unmodified as baseline generators throughout the paper's empirical evaluation, with GReaT shown to outperform them on most datasets.

title: Large Language Models(LLMs) on Tabular Data: Prediction, Generation, and Understanding -- A Survey

It situates LLM-based approaches against traditional and deep-learning synthetic data methods, positioning Copula-based and GAN-based generators as prior art before the modern generative-model era. title: Large Language Models as Realistic Microservice Trace Generators

It demonstrates that the generated traces can replace real data for microservice management tasks like heavy-hitter prediction and anomaly detection, outperforming prior structured-data generation baselines. title: Lost in the Averages: A New Specific Setup to Evaluate Membership Inference Attacks Against Machine Learning Models

summary: This paper develops a machine-learning framework (MLP, Random Forest, XGBoost) to predict bluebottle (Physalia) beaching events in Eastern Sydney, addressing class imbalance, class overlap, and unreliable absence labels through data augmentation strategies including SMOTE, random undersampling, and a novel 'Synthetic Negative Approach'.
